description:
WHAT THIS CASE PINS: 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN is ANSWERED, and the answer is a response that has no two-character batch equivalent - a length error - so the status is reported under COBOL's '9' permanent-error convention rather than as a fabricated two-digit code. This is the case that reaches the OTHER arm of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, the one no numeric-status case in this folder can: app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:162-163 tests IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9', and a status whose first byte is '9' carries a BINARY feedback code in its second byte rather than a digit. :164 moves IO-STAT1 into position one of IO-STATUS-04 - declared at :57-59 as IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 - :165 zeroes TWO-BYTES-BINARY, :166 overwrites its low-order byte with IO-STAT2, :167 moves the result into IO-STATUS-0403, and :168 DISPLAYs the literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by that four-character image. The feedback byte is binary zero, because a translated data-access failure carries no VSAM feedback code to report and inventing one would put a number into a job log that no backend produced, so the image is '9000'. THE TRAILING NNNN IS PART OF THE COBOL LITERAL at :168 and :172 - it is not a placeholder awaiting substitution, and 'correcting' it to the status value is the easiest way to fail this case. THE OPEN GUARD, WALKED ONCE: :119 MOVE 8 TO APPL-RESULT states the assumed failure before the attempt is made; :120 OPEN INPUT CARDFILE-FILE; :121 IF CARDFILE-STATUS = '00' is TWO-ARMED, so every status other than '00' - this one included - takes :124 MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT; :126's IF APPL-AOK is then false, so :129 DISPLAYs 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE', :130 moves CARDFILE-STATUS into IO-STATUS, :131 PERFORMs 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS and :132 PERFORMs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, which DISPLAYs 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :155, moves 999 into ABCODE at :157 and CALLs 'CEE3ABD' at :158. That call becomes an AbendException carrying RETURN-CODE 12 (gate G35) - the same 12 that :124 moves here, :101 moves on the read path and :142 reaches by ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING on the close path. WHAT IS THEREFORE NEVER EMITTED, asserted by its absence: the PERFORM UNTIL at :74-81 is never entered, so there is NO 150-character record image; 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE at :83 never runs, so no endBrowse is issued; and :85's end banner never appears. A run that printed the end banner after an abend would have escaped the CALL at :158, and the shape of this fingerprint - a fourth line that is an abend notice and not a banner - is what catches it. MESSAGE ARITHMETIC: 1 start banner + 1 open-error line + 1 status line + 1 abend line = 4 ordered DISPLAY_LINE entries, of 38, 22, 24 and 16 characters. There is no fifth entry and no 150-character entry. THE STATUS MATRIX THIS CASE COMPLETES: at the open, case08 forces '10' and case16 forces '22', both digits and both rendered by the NUMERIC arm at :170-172 as '0010' and '0022', while this case and case10 render '9000' through the arm at :164-168. The distinction between the two '9000' cases is the ROUTE and not the image: here the backend answers, with a length error, whereas in case10 the CARDFILE binding cannot be resolved at all and the backend never answers. case13 is this case's counterpart on the read side - an invalid-request response renders the same '9000' image through the same paragraph, and the only difference in its fingerprint is 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' at :110 in place of 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' at :129. That one image standing for three different responses is the point rather than a duplication, because 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS has exactly ONE non-numeric arm and every untranslatable response must land on it. THE INPUT IS A WELL-FORMED DATASET THAT IS NEVER READ. The two rows are written INLINE, byte for byte, from app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt rows 1 and 2 - keys 0500024453765740 and 0683586198171516, strictly ascending as the fixture holds them - so this file carries the record geometry itself rather than pointing at it. Seeding a fully well-formed, correctly-keyed dataset and then failing the OPEN is the assertion: the failure is in the OPEN and not in the data, and no amount of valid input rescues a status other than '00' from :121's two-armed guard. RECORD GEOMETRY, taken mechanically from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy (RECLN 150), one-based and cumulative so a reviewer can check this file against the copybook without running anything: CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, which is also the RECORD KEY at :32; CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 17-27; CARD-CVV-CD 9(03) at 28-30; CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME X(50) at 31-80; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 81-90, carrying the copybook's own misspelling, never corrected; CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 91; and FILLER X(59) at 92-150. The six NAMED fields stop at 91 and the FILLER carries everything after it: 91 + 59 = 150, and 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150 (gate G19). Row 1 decomposes to 0500024453765740, then 00000000050, then 747, then 'Aniya Von' followed by 41 spaces, then 2023-03-09, then Y, then 59 spaces; row 2 to 0683586198171516, then 00000000027, then 567, then 'Ward Jones' followed by 40 spaces, then 2025-07-13, then Y, then 59 spaces. All fifty rows of carddata.txt carry the same blank FILLER span, verified across the whole fixture, so every row of that file ends in a space. THE 59 TRAILING SPACES IN THIS FILE ARE LOAD-BEARING, AND THIS IS THE WARNING TO WHOEVER EDITS IT NEXT (gate G21). An editor, a formatter or a JSON tool that strips trailing whitespace turns each 150-character row into a 91-character one, and that is not a cosmetic change: FILLER is a FIRST-CLASS SPAN in the fixed-width record layer, which self-checks that its declared spans sum to the record length, so a dropped span fails immediately and every offset past 91 in every consumer of the record is wrong. The suite catches it at once, because every seeded row of every case in this folder is asserted at exactly 150 characters, and the differ quotes images so that a difference in trailing spaces alone is visible rather than invisible. FILLER is emitted because the COBOL emits it; it is not empty padding that can be dropped. WHERE THE DISPLAYED-IMAGE CLAIMS LIVE, since this case emits none: case05 reads these same two rows to RETURN-CODE 0 and four lines of 38, 150, 150 and 36 characters; case17 pins the blank FILLER of a single inline row; case18 pins a zoned overpunch inside the FILLER surviving verbatim; case19 pins two inline rows at the extremes of every declared field. This case is the '9000' open-side counterpart and deliberately does not duplicate any of them. WHAT A REVIEWER MUST NOT TRUST: the unit under test is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob - an Account-named class in the account package - yet CBACT02C reads the CARD file and never touches the account file. :29-33 is SELECT CARDFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO CARDFILE, ORGANIZATION INDEXED, ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY FD-CARD-NUM, over an FD of FD-CARD-NUM X(16) plus FD-CARD-DATA X(134) = 150, and :45 is COPY CVACT02Y. AAP rule R1 governs - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and the divergence is catalogued in the register at AAP 0.8.4. A reviewer who trusts the class name authors the wrong twenty cases. IN REPOSITORY TERMS the sequence is one openBrowse answering with a response that translates to no two-character status, and then nothing at all: no readNext and no endBrowse, because the abend leaves the program from inside 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN (gate G47). The other statuses this same call site can report are covered around it - '10' by case08, '22' by case16 and '00' by every clean case - while '23' and this untranslatable response are additionally driven at unit level by AccountBalanceReaderJobTest.OpenStatusLadder, so the two-armed guard is exercised from both directions. The job is driven at tasklet/step level, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). WIRING: app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare //STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C, the job declares no PARM anywhere and the program has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one, so jobParameters is empty; its single //CARDFILE DD at :25-26 is the only dataset, addressed here by the CARDFILE binding key that application.yml resolves at record length 150 and never by a dataset name, so no DSNAME literal appears in this file (gate G46). NOTHING IS WRITTEN: expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty because :120 opens INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE - SYSOUT at READCARD.jcl:27 is its only output - and here the abend means not even a read is attempted. No normalisation is declared, because carddata.txt rows are already the full 150 bytes CVACT02Y declares, unlike cardxref.txt whose 36-byte rows need a 14-byte pad. ENCODING is US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default. PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for each offset and width, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and DD contract, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the two seeded rows. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: AAP 0.7.6 proves that impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot be made executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator plus three absent IBM copybooks, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler installable - and the substitution is recorded as risk R-A. Two well-formed 150-byte records in, four diagnostic lines out, no record image, no end banner, RETURN-CODE 12.

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges an OPEN that reports DFHRESP(LENGERR), a response with no two-character batch equivalent, so the status becomes the permanent-error convention: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names OPEN-CARDFILE and gives it RESP 22. It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the shape used to be chosen by a switch over 'case01'..'case20' in CBACT02CParityTest, so this file showed the abend lines and said nothing about the condition that produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site reads its whole input and closes cleanly, so silence here is itself a statement. The outcome is a CICS RESP rather than a FILE STATUS because CardRepository reports this program's card-file outcomes as responses and AccountBalanceReaderJob translates them - declaring a status directly would skip the translation the case exists to judge.
